Chapter 2. The Unexpected Path: From Village Life to the Dance Academy.
Imagine this: one ordinary morning, the usual rhythm of village life is suddenly broken by a big announcement at school. City officials have shown up, looking for kids to join a special new program. Teachers who are normally strict and distant are now scanning the classroom with keen eyes, searching for potential stars. The criteria? Well, that's a bit mysterious—physical ability, discipline, loyalty to the Party. Nobody really knows what that means, and honestly, most of the kids are on edge, not sure what to expect.
The selection process is both thrilling and a little bit scary. The officials ask everyone to do simple things—touch your toes, jump, answer questions about your family and what you believe in. For many, it's the first time they've ever been picked out for anything.
Now, our boy—usually the quiet type, the one who likes to blend in—feels caught between hope and fear. He wants nothing more than to make his parents proud, but the idea of leaving home? That’s just as terrifying as it is exciting.
After several rounds of these tests, only a handful of children are chosen to travel to the city for more evaluation. The journey itself is overwhelming. The city is noisy, packed with people, and full of sights that are completely foreign. The buildings seem to stretch into the sky, and everyone moves with a purpose. For a kid from the countryside, it almost feels like stepping onto another planet.
When they reach the final selection, the real stakes become clear. This isn’t just any school—it’s a highly respected dance academy, run by the government. The training is intense, the expectations sky-high. Only a select few will get in, and those who do will be expected to dedicate their lives to dance, representing the country as cultural ambassadors.
The boy feels torn. Leaving his family behind feels nearly impossible, but this opportunity? It’s once in a lifetime. His parents, though their hearts are breaking, encourage him to take the chance. They see it as a way out—a shot at a better future. His mother, especially, tries to hide her tears and tells her son to be brave.
The first days at the academy are a total shock to the system. The schedule is tough—long hours of physical training, schoolwork, and political study. The teachers? Demanding and quick to point out mistakes, but slow to give out praise. The other students come from all over the country. Some are just as homesick, while others are fiercely ambitious.
At first, the boy struggles. His body isn’t as flexible as some of the others, and his technique still needs a lot of work. The homesickness is intense—every night, he dreams about his family, their faces blurred by distance. The food is strange, the rules are strict, and mistakes aren’t easily forgiven. There’s barely any room for weakness.
But slowly, things begin to shift. What once felt like harsh discipline starts to become a source of strength. He learns how to push through the pain, to focus on small wins. He finds mentors—older students and even a few teachers—who notice his determination and offer advice. The shared struggle creates friendships, making the loneliness just a little bit easier to bear.
Letters from home quickly become his lifeline. His mother’s words, always full of encouragement and love, remind him why he’s here. His father’s quiet pride comes through in every sentence, even if he doesn’t say much. The sacrifices his family has made are always on his mind, and that gives him the drive to keep going.
Over time, something beautiful happens. The boy discovers a passion for dance he never saw coming. The movements, once awkward and forced, start to feel natural. The music stirs up emotions he can’t quite put into words. The stage? It becomes a place where he can finally express himself, free from the limitations of language.
The academy isn’t just a school—it’s a crucible. Here, students are shaped by challenges, strengthened by discipline, and inspired by the dream of something bigger. For the boy, it becomes clear: this journey, as hard as it is, offers a way to honor his family’s hopes and, maybe, to find his own voice in a world that so rarely listens to the dreams of the poor.
